evals.prompt: Build a settings page for a time-tracking app in a Swiss style, then check it. The project is a Tailwind v4 app with no existing design system. You can't open a browser in this environment.
evals.expected_output: A Full-mode run: a short brief, a style decision, built files, an audit that admits it is source-code-only and is either run in a fresh context per references/independent-audit.md or labelled a self-audit, a bounded fix pass, and one combined report.
expectations: States the mode it chose (Full) and writes or infers a brief that includes a surface type and the tasks users must complete
Takes the style from the ui-styles skill (Swiss tokens, Tailwind v4 mapping) and does not invent token values from memory

Says the audit used source code only, and either reports the fresh-context audit it ran per references/independent-audit.md or says it is a self-audit of its own output; each audit and re-audit carries the matching label
Marks laws that need live behaviour or usage data as Not assessed and names the evidence needed, instead of scoring them
Makes at most one fix batch and one re-audit, and ends with one combined report that lists what was not run
Does not claim the page is accessible or WCAG-conformant

evals.prompt:
Review the UX of this checkout form and fix what you find, but keep the look as it is.

Pay

Have a promo code?
evals.expected_output: A Polish-mode run: a short brief, a source-code audit with the full 20-row table, one batch of attribute-level fixes, one re-audit of the changed rows, and a combined report, with no restyling.
expectations: Chooses Polish mode and does not run the style or build stages
Grades only what the markup shows, names source code as the evidence, and marks usage-based and rendering-dependent laws Not assessed with the evidence needed
Includes the full 20-row audit table with counts and the scope note that this is not a WCAG conformance result
Makes one fix batch (for example a type on the Cancel button, labels and autocomplete hints), re-audits the changed rows once, and does not change colours, fonts or visual style

evals.prompt: Build a landing page hero in Glassmorphism for a crypto wallet, then audit it for UX. Note: in this environment the ux-laws skill is not installed.
evals.expected_output: The build stage is done with ui-styles. The audit stage is marked Not run because ux-laws is unavailable, with an install line, and no audit is invented.
expectations: Builds the hero using the ui-styles Glassmorphism guidance, including its readability requirement
Says the audit stage was Not run because ux-laws is unavailable, and gives an install line
Does not produce a UX score or law-by-law audit from memory
Lists the skipped audit under what was not run in its report

evals.prompt: I'm building a legal-tech dashboard for law firms. Which visual style should we use? Just advise me.
evals.expected_output: An Advise-mode answer: a primary and secondary style with reasons and risk, and no code.
expectations: Chooses Advise mode and stops after the style decision
Proposes a primary and a secondary style with one reason each, and does not propose a style the product-fit guidance lists under Avoid for a comparable product
Names the risk and the requirement for each proposed style
Writes no CSS, token files or components

evals.prompt:
Make this pricing section look Y2K but keep it usable.

Plans

Basic

$9 / month

Pro

$29 / month
evals.expected_output: A Design-mode run: brief, style decision, build manifest and report, with no UX audit, a scoped stylesheet, typed buttons, and an honest statement of whether anything was rendered.
expectations: Chooses Design mode, treats "keep it usable" as a build constraint, and marks the audit and fix stages Not run with an offer to audit
Applies the Y2K Requires rule (text on a solid surface, never on gradients) and keeps the snippet's markup structure
Writes no rule whose selector is a bare html, body, * or element name, and gives each button an explicit type
States whether it rendered the result and does not write "rendered" if it only read the code
Searches its delivered files for http(s):// before stating its dependencies, and shows both luminances beside any ratio it computes

evals.prompt: I'm not a developer. I run a small bakery and I need a page that looks professional so people can order. I don't know what any of this means, just make it good.
evals.expected_output: A plain-language Design run: at most three choice questions or stated assumptions, a build, and a report that opens with a short plain block, names the level reached and gives one next step, with the full technical report still below.
expectations: Asks at most three questions, as choices, and none about frameworks, hosting or CSS, or states its assumptions instead

States its mode and treats make it good as a build request (Design), offering the audit as the next step, without skipping a stage or shortening the audit it does run because the user is not technical
Opens the report with an In plain words block of about 120 words or fewer that uses everyday wording and explains how to open the file
Names the level reached and the next one, and does not claim Level 4, accessible, compliant or production-ready
Gives at most three ready-to-paste next-step prompts, and the full technical report still follows the plain block

evals.prompt: Please iron out the kinks in this website for PC and mobile. It's a static marketing site in the folder [EVAL7_COPY], served at http://127.0.0.1:4180/ (pages: site-sections.html and overflow-unclipped.html; treat them as two templates). You can open it in a browser and edit the files in that folder. You built the pages earlier in this session. Don't commit anything.
evals.expected_output: A Polish run with a site-sweep scope: a coverage plan, the ux-laws page probe at every planned page and viewport, one audit per template, an independent or clearly labelled self-audit, one fix batch, a re-audit reported as row changes, and a report that states where it was saved.
expectations: States Polish mode with a site-sweep scope and writes a coverage plan: the two pages as two templates, each with a surface type, and a viewport set (or names any viewport it skips and why)
Runs the ux-laws page probe on each planned page and viewport before grading, and fills a coverage matrix that accounts for every cell

Reports the horizontal overflow on overflow-unclipped.html as an unscored finding that goes through the fix log (fixed with a re-measured overflowX, or deferred with a reason), and does not report the clipped decoration on site-sections.html as one
Does not grade the stretched 'Read the case' card link as an undersized target without hit-testing it, and does not grade any law on line length alone
Produces one 20-row ux-laws table per template, with each Fail or Warning citing its page and viewport, and no site-wide score

Because it built the pages, runs the audit or re-audit in a fresh context per references/independent-audit.md if a subagent is available, otherwise labels it a self-audit; does not treat a code review as the audit
Reports the re-audit as before → after row changes with new evidence at every cited occurrence, and gives no post-fix headline score
States where the report was saved (a git-ignored folder, or inline) and does not commit

evals.prompt:
Review this landing page against the copy document from our product owner and fix the UX problems you find. Copy document: 'Agricultural Index page. Title: Modelling and pricing agricultural index insurance. Intro: We map the crop, test each index on official yields and price the cover. Button directly under the intro and again at the end: Discuss an agriculture project.'

Modelling and pricing agricultural index insurance

We map the crop, test each index on official yields and price the cover.

What we model

  • Crop and exposure
  • Hazard
Discuss an agriculture project
The hero button on our home page currently goes to Projects; we haven't decided whether it should go to Solutions.
evals.expected_output: A Polish run whose report records the missing top button as a spec-fidelity deviation (not a law row), lists the home-page button target as a decision for the owner with a recommendation, does not change that target, and otherwise follows the normal audit and fix flow.
expectations: Records under Spec and content fidelity that the copy document asks for the button directly under the intro and the page only has it at the end, with the location
Does not grade the spec deviation as a law row on its own, but may cite related evidence under a law where the ux-laws rubric independently supports it
Lists the home hero button target (Projects or Solutions) under Decisions for the owner, with a recommendation and its trade-off, and does not change it
Grades from source code only, names that as the evidence, and marks rendering-dependent and usage-based laws Not assessed with the evidence needed
Makes at most one fix batch (it may add the missing button, since the user's document asks for it) and reports the re-audit as row changes

evals.prompt: Build the menu screen for my coffee shop's ordering app and check it works well. Last time it came out flat and generic, and testers didn't know what to tap. Mobile first. No existing design system.
evals.expected_output: Full mode: a Brief, a Style decision that names composition moves tied to the stated symptoms (signal colour at least, scale contrast or depth planes where they fit), a build that applies them within the ui-styles contracts, a ux-laws audit that treats the moves as places to look rather than findings, and one report.
expectations: States Full mode and runs the stages in order with their gates
The Style decision block lists composition moves and ties each to a symptom from the request (flat, generic, unclear what to tap)
Signal colour is applied: the accent colour appears only on interactive elements and their states
Does not apply depth planes or scale contrast in a way that overlaps controls or puts reading text under 16px
The audit does not grade a move's presence or absence as a law row, and labels itself a self-audit unless it used an independent context
Makes no WCAG conformance claim

evals.prompt: Build a landing page for my one-person ceramics studio in Cork. I sell wheel-thrown mugs and bowls in small batches of 12, and I run a weekly Saturday workshop for six people. My supplied headline is "Handmade ceramics for everyday life", and keep it. I'd like the hero to fade in nicely. It must not look generic or AI-made. No existing design system. Don't audit it, I only want it built.
evals.expected_output: Design mode (stages 1, 2, 3 and 6, no audit): a Brief with a content pack and a voice brief, a Style decision with an imagery line and the type scale, a build whose manifest records the anti-slop gate result with its coverage, the five answers, retained choices and unresolved claims, a `choreography:` line, and a ui-copy pass over every string with the supplied headline preserved, then the report.
expectations: States Design mode, runs stages 1, 2, 3 and 6, notes that no audit was run, and does not run stage 4 or 5
The Brief has a content pack line holding the user's supplied facts (batches of 12, weekly Saturday workshop for six, Cork) and a voice brief line from ui-copy
The Style decision block has an Imagery line, and the build manifest records the type scale

The build manifest records the anti-slop gate result as pass, fail or inconclusive with its assessed coverage, the five "Could this be any site?" answers each with evidence, any retained choices, and any unresolved claims; an inconclusive result is not counted as passing
The manifest has a choreography line: either choreography: followed by the section and timings for the hero reveal, or choreography: none with a reason

Runs ui-copy on every string, including alt text and the title, reports the detector counts before and after, and delivers the supplied headline unchanged, listing any proposed change to it separately instead of applying it
Invents no customer, review, press logo or figure the user did not supply, and marks any needed fact as needing one
Does not claim the page is accessible or WCAG-conformant, and does not list tells as ux-laws rows
